items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Willow Hall, Executive Director, G2G Rail Trail Inc. and Jill Murray-Dimic, Ontario Conservation Accelerator
notes:
Willow Hall, Executive Director of G2G Rail Trail Inc., discussed the community impact of a new pedestrian bridge along the Guelph-to-Goderich trail. W. Hall noted the bridge would provide a safe, accessible trail, build tourism, and support both economic and community growth. He also noted that $5.5 million out of the estimated $8.26 million total project costs has been covered by two (2) private donors.

W. Hall requested that Council support the recommended design and next steps to move the project forward. 

Jill Murray-Dimic, Director of Fundraising, gave a summary of the community donations received and noted that with Regional support, the project could begin later this year. 

In response to a question from Committee, W. Hall noted there were193,000 unique visits recorded in 2025. 

In a response to a question from Committee regarding the economic benefit of the bridge, W. Hall noted cycle tourism as a major source. 

In respone to a question from Committee about the potential for further fundraising, W. Hall noted that hundreds of donations have been received, and that more fundraising would delay plans, disrupt the timeline, and potentially lose the interest of the private donors. 

Committee raised concerns over the future infrastructure costs related to the project. Responding to Committee, W. Hall stated he believed that ongoing maintenance costs are likely to be funded through community donors. 

W. Hall confirmed ongoing work with Explore Waterloo. Responding to Committee, W. Hall stated a majority of out-of-Region visitors come from Guelph or Toronto, and that the G2G Rail Trail is gaining international recognition. 

Committee acknowledged the safety improvements the proposed bridge would bring to the trail.

Responding to Committee, W. Hall confirmed that the Region's support for this project could be recognized on map boards, trail heads and parking lot signage.

items.title: EES-DCS-26-001, G2G Pedestrian Bridge Over the Conestoga River, Wallenstein
notes:
Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner of Transportation Services, introduced this report. . 

Responding to Committee, M. Goetzke noted the 75-year lifespan of the bridge is well beyond the 10-year capital program. He confirmed that the Region of Waterloo would be the owner of the asset, and therefore responsible for future maintainence costs. 

Committee raised concerns over a longterm plan for infrastructure management.

Responding to Committee, Wayne Steffler, Commissioner of Corporate Services, stated the project is recommended to be funded out of the capital tax reserve. He further explained that as a new asset, it would get added to the Asset Management Plan and maintainence costs would be funded through the capital budget.

items.title: EES-DCS-26-002, 2026 Upcoming Regional Road Construction
notes:
Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner of Transportation Services, provided Committee with an update on upcoming regional road construction. 

In response to Committee, M. Goetzke explained how Bill 60 contains restriction for the current plan for cycling lanes on Frederick Street reconstruction project. M. Goetzke stated staff is working with the Ministry of Transportation to understand the full scope of the bill and consulting with area municipalities to plan accordingly. 

In response to a question from Committee, M. Goetzke spoke on communication outlets, and highlighted EngageWR as a good single source for information. 

In response to Committee, Frank Cosa, Director of Design and Constuction, confirmed work near the Scheifele Bridge will be completed in phases to allow roads to remain open. 

In response to Committee, M. Goetzke explained that the Townships are part of a single rural resurfracing contract, which is why they are lumped together. He stated that the Townships can be seperated in future reports so that more clarity is be provided.  

In response to a question from Committee, M. Goetzke that information on the work on Schneider Road can be brought back to Committee. 

In respose to concerns from Committee, M. Goetzke stated staff are working with police services in regards to the fatal accident on Cedar Street. He confirmed a root cause report will be provided to Council following the police investigation. 

Committee voiced concerns on various projects not included in the report.

In response to a question to Committee, Connie MacDonald confirmed positive trends in the uptake of the piloted text notification program and plans to continue expanding in 2026.

items.title: Other Business
notes:
Councillor Wolf raised concerns over the maintenance of the Hydrocut and asked for clarification on tree removal practices.  

In response to Committee, Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, clarified that considerable consultation was done during planning. 

Councillor Huinink spoke about Mobility Plus lap belt policy and general restrictions. In response, Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner of Transportation Services, confirmed that staff outreach to affected users has happened and that more information on this issue will be provided to Council. 

Chair James requested further clarification on Ion speed. M. Goetzke confirmed staff are working on this issue. M. Goetzke further clarified the limitations on automatic train protection system and the work being done on crossings, switch repair, and transit signal priority.

motions.item_title: PDL-LEG-26-016, Expropriate Land (2nd Report) for Improvements to Fischer Hallman (between Bleams-Plains)
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for improvements to Fischer Hallman Road between Bleams Road and Plains Road, in the City of Kitchener, in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, as detailed in Report PDL-LEG-26-016, dated April 7, 2026, described as follows: Temporary Easement: The right and easement, being a temporary easement in gross, for the free and unobstructed, right, interest and easement terminating, for the subject properties set out below, on the 31 st day of December 2028, for itself, its successors and assigns, and anyone authorized by it, on, over, under and through the following property for the purposes of excavation, construction, installation, replacement, alteration, grading, and landscaping as required in connection with the improvements to Fischer Hallman Road between Bleams Road and Plains Road, and all related improvements, and works ancillary thereto and for such purposes, the free, unimpeded and unobstructed access to the lands at all times by employees, agents, contractors, workers and anyone authorized by it, and vehicles, supplies and equipment at all times and for all purposes and things necessary for or incidental to the exercise and enjoyment of the right and easement: Part of the Common Element, Waterloo Standard Condominium Plan 566, being Parts 1, 2, 3 and 4 on 58R-22432, City of Kitchener, part of PINs 23566-0001 to 23566-0276, (1652 – 1696 Fischer Hallman Road, Kitchener); Part of Lot 158, German Company Tract, being Part 7 on 58R-19936, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22607-2288, (945 Huron Road, Kitchener); Part of Lot 5, Registrar’s Compiled Plan 1471, being Parts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 on 58R-22500, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22607-2322, (1340 Fischer Hallman Road, Kitchener); Part of Lot 6, Registrar’s Compiled Plan 1471, being Part 7 on 58R-22500, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22607-2454, (Part of Vacant Land, Fischer Hallman Road, Kitchener); and Part of Lot 156, German Company Tract, being Part 3 on 58R-19941, City of Kitchener, part of PIN 22607-2317, (1548 Fischer Hallman Road, Kitchener) And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the properties within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the properties, as required by the Expropriations Act; And that the registered owners for the properties be served with a Notice of Expropriation, Notice of Election and a Notice of Possession after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act; And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required; And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the properties in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act ; And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation; And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner, Engineering & Environmental Services, that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project.
